section_summary.extract_value: This abstract reports a single study in which 92 female college students completed nightly online questionnaires for seven days to examine how exposure to non-body focused versus body focused others affected eating and body image. Between-persons, greater exposure to non-body focused others predicted better outcomes (greater intuitive eating, greater body appreciation, less dietary restraint) while exposure to body focused others predicted the opposite; within-persons effects were found for non-body focused others but not body focused others. The section does not report country, age, racial composition, BMI, or the specific instruments used to assess body appreciation.
